report.summary: Your blood report shows several abnormal values that need prompt attention. Out of 15 parameters analyzed, 7 were outside the normal reference range. 1 possible deficiency indicator(s) were flagged. This report is for informational purposes only and does not replace professional medical advice.
critical_alerts: HbA1c is critically low (3.14 %) — please consult a doctor promptly.
report.doctor_consultation_reason: One or more parameters are in the critical range.

deficiencies.title: Low Vitamin D
deficiencies.explanation: Your Vitamin D (4.8 ng/mL) is below the healthy reference range, which may indicate a deficiency. Supports bone health and immunity; low levels are very common.

health_risks.title: Hemoglobin out of range
health_risks.explanation: Your Hemoglobin (18.2 g/dL) is above the healthy reference range. Carries oxygen in your blood. Low levels can mean anemia and cause fatigue.

health_risks.title: WBC Count out of range
health_risks.explanation: Your WBC Count (0.6 10^3/uL) is below the healthy reference range. White blood cells fight infection; high counts can signal infection or inflammation.

health_risks.title: HbA1c out of range
health_risks.explanation: Your HbA1c (3.14 %) is below the healthy reference range. Reflects your average blood sugar over the last ~3 months.

health_risks.title: Total Cholesterol out of range
health_risks.explanation: Your Total Cholesterol (247.34 mg/dL) is above the healthy reference range. A measure of fats in your blood linked to heart disease risk.

health_risks.title: LDL Cholesterol out of range
health_risks.explanation: Your LDL Cholesterol (113.64 mg/dL) is above the healthy reference range. 'Bad' cholesterol — high levels raise heart disease risk.

health_risks.title: SGPT (ALT) out of range
health_risks.explanation: Your SGPT (ALT) (1.05 U/L) is below the healthy reference range. A liver enzyme; elevated levels can indicate liver stress or damage.

parameter_explanations.Hemoglobin: Carries oxygen in your blood. Low levels can mean anemia and cause fatigue.
parameter_explanations.WBC Count: White blood cells fight infection; high counts can signal infection or inflammation.
parameter_explanations.Platelet Count: Platelets help your blood clot; very low or high counts need medical attention.
parameter_explanations.Fasting Blood Glucose: Blood sugar after fasting; consistently high levels can indicate prediabetes/diabetes.
parameter_explanations.HbA1c: Reflects your average blood sugar over the last ~3 months.
parameter_explanations.Total Cholesterol: A measure of fats in your blood linked to heart disease risk.
parameter_explanations.LDL Cholesterol: 'Bad' cholesterol — high levels raise heart disease risk.
parameter_explanations.HDL Cholesterol: 'Good' cholesterol — higher levels help protect your heart.
parameter_explanations.Triglycerides: A type of fat in blood; high levels are linked to heart disease.
parameter_explanations.TSH: Signals your thyroid to produce hormones; abnormal levels affect metabolism.
parameter_explanations.Vitamin D: Supports bone health and immunity; low levels are very common.
parameter_explanations.Vitamin B12: Needed for nerve function and red blood cell production.
parameter_explanations.Serum Creatinine: A waste product filtered by kidneys; high levels can signal reduced kidney function.
parameter_explanations.SGPT (ALT): A liver enzyme; elevated levels can indicate liver stress or damage.
parameter_explanations.Calcium: Important for bones, muscles, and nerve function.
